title: Aligning a Tier Exception Approval with the Member's Other Exception Approvals (Formulary Benefit)
content:
Under the Formulary Benefit, the starting period of a tier exception approval is aligned with the member's other exception approvals, so that they come up for renewal together. The member's exception approvals of any drug are read, with their expiration dates.

**In force.** An approval is in force on the decision date when the latest expiration date among the member's approvals is the decision date or later.

**Clause.**
1. An approval is in force, and the latest expiration date is at least **6** whole months after the decision date (the alignment minimum). The starting tier period is those whole months plus one, so that it ends in the same month.
2. An approval is in force, but its latest expiration is fewer than 6 whole months away. The starting tier period is those whole months plus one plus the renewal cycle of **12** months.
3. In every other case, the starting tier period is the formulary's standard approval length, which is **12** months on every Northbridge formulary.

The tier approval period is worked from this starting period. The floor of one month applies only to the finished period.

## Worked cases (hypothetical decision date of 10 March 2026)

| Latest expiration among the member's approvals | Whole months away | Starting tier period |
|---|---|---|
| 14 November 2026 | 8 | 8 plus 1, which is 9 |
| 10 September 2026 | 6 | 6 plus 1, which is 7 |
| 20 May 2026 | 2 | 2 plus 1 plus 12, which is 15 |
| 1 March 2026 (already expired) | | 12 |
| no approval on record | | 12 |
